1.headline: A court in Nigeria stops a top candidate
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
Today's news is from Nigeria. Nigeria is a big country in Africa. It will have an election for president soon.
On Thursday, a court made a big decision. It stopped a top candidate. His name is Atiku Abubakar. He is a former vice president.
The judge said something about his party. The party chose its leaders in the wrong way. So the court said the party's choice of him does not count.
His party is angry. It says it will go to a higher court. It wants the decision changed.
The vote is about two months away. Many people are watching.
Again, a court in Nigeria stopped a top candidate for president. His party will fight the decision.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스입니다.
오늘의 뉴스는 나이지리아 소식입니다. 나이지리아는 아프리카의 큰 나라입니다. 곧 대통령 선거가 열립니다.
목요일에 한 법원이 중요한 결정을 내렸습니다. 법원은 유력 후보 한 명을 막았습니다. 그의 이름은 아티쿠 아부바카르입니다. 그는 전직 부통령입니다.
판사는 그의 정당에 대해 말했습니다. 그 정당이 지도부를 잘못된 방식으로 뽑았다는 것입니다. 그래서 법원은 정당이 그를 후보로 고른 것이 인정되지 않는다고 했습니다.
그의 정당은 화가 나 있습니다. 정당은 더 높은 법원에 가겠다고 말합니다. 결정이 바뀌기를 원합니다.
투표는 약 두 달 뒤에 있습니다. 많은 사람이 지켜보고 있습니다.
다시 말씀드리면, 나이지리아의 한 법원이 유력 대통령 후보를 막았습니다. 그의 정당은 이 결정에 맞서 싸울 것입니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

2.headline: Nigerian court cancels a top candidate's run for president
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
Today's story is from Nigeria, a large country in West Africa. Nigeria will choose a new president next year. But a court has just removed one of the top candidates.

On Thursday, a judge in Abuja, the capital city, made the decision. The candidate is Atiku Abubakar. He was once Nigeria's vice president. He is running for an opposition party. That means a party that is not in power.
The judge said the party chose its leaders illegally. Because of this, the party's choice of Atiku was not valid. News reports say the ruling also cancels the party's other candidates.
The party says it will appeal. To appeal means to ask a higher court to change a decision. The party and some critics say the ruling party was behind the case.
Why is this important? The vote is about two months away, according to the Associated Press. Nigeria also has money problems and growing violence. This ruling makes the election more complicated.
To sum up, a Nigerian court cancelled Atiku Abubakar's run for president, and his party plans to appeal.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스입니다.
오늘의 소식은 서아프리카의 큰 나라 나이지리아에서 왔습니다. 나이지리아는 내년에 새 대통령을 뽑습니다. 그런데 한 법원이 유력 후보 한 명을 막 제외했습니다.
목요일에 수도 아부자의 한 판사가 이 결정을 내렸습니다. 후보는 아티쿠 아부바카르입니다. 그는 한때 나이지리아 부통령이었습니다. 그는 야당 후보로 나섰습니다. 야당은 권력을 잡지 않은 정당을 말합니다.
판사는 그 정당이 지도부를 불법으로 뽑았다고 말했습니다. 이 때문에 정당이 아티쿠를 후보로 고른 것도 효력이 없다고 했습니다. 보도에 따르면 이번 판결은 그 정당의 다른 후보들도 취소합니다.
정당은 항소하겠다고 말합니다. 항소란 더 높은 법원에 결정을 바꿔 달라고 요청하는 것입니다. 정당과 일부 비판자들은 집권당이 이 소송의 배후에 있다고 말합니다.
이것이 왜 중요할까요? AP 통신에 따르면 투표는 약 두 달 뒤입니다. 나이지리아는 경제 문제와 늘어나는 폭력도 겪고 있습니다. 이번 판결로 선거가 더 복잡해졌습니다.
정리하면, 나이지리아 법원이 아티쿠 아부바카르의 대선 출마를 취소했고, 그의 정당은 항소할 계획입니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

3.headline: Nigerian court voids leading opposition candidate's bid
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.

Today's story comes from Nigeria, the country with the largest population in Africa. A court there has removed a leading candidate from next year's presidential election. According to news reports, a judge at the Federal High Court in Abuja, the capital, made the ruling on Thursday.

The candidate is Atiku Abubakar, a former vice president of Nigeria. He was running for the African Democratic Congress, an opposition party. An opposition party is a party that is not in power. The judge said the party's current leaders were put in place illegally. Because of this, the court said the party's choice of Atiku was not valid. Reports say the ruling also cancels the party's other candidates for the 2027 elections.

The case was brought by one of the party's own deputy leaders. He argued that he should have taken over as party leader. The party says it will appeal. To appeal means to ask a higher court to change a decision. The party and some critics claim the ruling party was behind the case.

This is not the party's first trip to court. Earlier this year, a court ordered the party to be removed from the official list of parties. A higher court overturned that order, which means it cancelled it.

Why does this matter? The vote is only about two months away, according to the Associated Press. Nigeria is also facing a troubled economy and rising violence. The ruling makes an already difficult election process more complicated, and the final answer may come from a higher court.
To sum up, a Nigerian court has cancelled Atiku Abubakar's presidential candidacy, and his party plans to appeal.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스입니다.
오늘의 소식은 아프리카에서 인구가 가장 많은 나라 나이지리아에서 왔습니다. 그곳의 한 법원이 내년 대통령 선거에서 유력 후보 한 명을 제외했습니다. 보도에 따르면 수도 아부자에 있는 연방고등법원의 한 판사가 목요일에 이 판결을 내렸습니다.

후보는 나이지리아의 전 부통령 아티쿠 아부바카르입니다. 그는 야당인 아프리카민주회의 후보로 나섰습니다. 야당은 권력을 잡지 않은 정당을 말합니다. 판사는 이 정당의 현 지도부가 불법으로 세워졌다고 말했습니다. 이 때문에 법원은 정당이 아티쿠를 후보로 고른 것이 효력이 없다고 했습니다. 보도에 따르면 이번 판결은 2027년 선거에 나설 이 정당의 다른 후보들도 취소합니다.
이 소송은 그 정당의 부대표 중 한 명이 제기했습니다. 그는 자신이 당 대표를 맡았어야 했다고 주장했습니다. 정당은 항소하겠다고 말합니다. 항소란 더 높은 법원에 결정을 바꿔 달라고 요청하는 것입니다. 정당과 일부 비판자들은 집권당이 이 소송의 배후에 있다고 주장합니다.
이 정당이 법원에 간 것은 처음이 아닙니다. 올해 초 한 법원은 이 정당을 공식 정당 명단에서 빼라고 명령했습니다. 상급 법원은 그 명령을 뒤집었습니다. 즉, 취소한 것입니다.
이것이 왜 중요할까요? AP 통신에 따르면 투표는 약 두 달밖에 남지 않았습니다. 나이지리아는 어려운 경제와 늘어나는 폭력에도 직면해 있습니다. 이번 판결로 이미 어려운 선거 과정이 더 복잡해졌고, 최종 결론은 상급 법원에서 나올 수도 있습니다.
정리하면, 나이지리아 법원이 아티쿠 아부바카르의 대통령 후보 자격을 취소했고, 그의 정당은 항소할 계획입니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

4.headline: Nigerian court voids Atiku Abubakar's presidential candidacy
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.

We begin in Nigeria, where a court has thrown the country's upcoming presidential election into fresh uncertainty. According to news reports, a judge at the Federal High Court in Abuja ruled on Thursday that the leadership of the opposition African Democratic Congress had been illegally constituted.

As a result, the court voided the candidacy of Atiku Abubakar, a former vice president of Nigeria and one of the country's best-known opposition figures. Nigerian media report that the judgment also nullified the nominations of the party's other candidates for the 2027 elections, along with the appointment of its national officers.

The lawsuit was filed by one of the party's deputy national chairmen, who argued that he should have taken over the leadership when the previous chairman resigned. The party has said it will appeal, and both party officials and critics accuse the ruling party of orchestrating the case.
This is not the first legal challenge the party has faced. Earlier this year, a court ordered it to be deregistered, but that decision was overturned on appeal.

Mr. Abubakar is a veteran of Nigerian politics who has run for the presidency several times before, including in 2023, when Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress won the election and became president.

The timing is especially significant. The Associated Press notes that the ruling comes roughly two months before the vote, in a country already struggling with a troubled economy and escalating insecurity. Observers will be watching closely to see whether a higher court restores Mr. Abubakar's candidacy before voters head to the polls. For now, many questions remain unanswered.
To sum up, a Nigerian federal court has disqualified opposition candidate Atiku Abubakar, and his party plans to challenge the ruling.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스에 오신 것을 환영합니다.
나이지리아 소식으로 시작합니다. 그곳의 한 법원이 다가오는 대통령 선거를 새로운 불확실성 속으로 몰아넣었습니다. 보도에 따르면 아부자 연방고등법원의 한 판사는 목요일, 야당 아프리카민주회의의 지도부가 불법으로 구성되었다고 판결했습니다.
그 결과 법원은 전 부통령이자 나이지리아에서 가장 잘 알려진 야권 인사 중 한 명인 아티쿠 아부바카르의 후보 자격을 무효로 했습니다. 나이지리아 언론은 이번 판결이 2027년 선거에 나설 이 정당의 다른 후보 지명과 전국 지도부 임명도 무효로 했다고 전했습니다.
소송은 이 정당의 전국 부대표 중 한 명이 제기했습니다. 그는 전임 대표가 사임했을 때 자신이 지도부를 이어받았어야 했다고 주장했습니다. 정당은 항소하겠다고 밝혔고, 당 관계자와 비판자들은 모두 집권당이 이 소송을 꾸몄다고 비난합니다.
이 정당이 법적 문제에 부딪힌 것은 처음이 아닙니다. 올해 초 한 법원은 이 정당의 등록을 취소하라고 명령했지만, 그 결정은 항소심에서 뒤집혔습니다.
아부바카르는 여러 차례 대선에 출마한 나이지리아 정계의 베테랑으로, 2023년 선거에도 나섰습니다. 그 선거에서는 전진보회의의 볼라 티누부가 승리해 대통령이 되었습니다.
시점이 중요합니다. AP 통신은 이번 판결이 투표를 약 두 달 앞두고 나왔다고 짚었습니다. 나이지리아는 이미 어려운 경제와 악화하는 치안 불안에 시달리고 있습니다. 관측통들은 유권자들이 투표하러 가기 전에 상급 법원이 아부바카르의 후보 자격을 되살릴지 주목할 것입니다. 지금으로서는 많은 질문이 답을 기다리고 있습니다.
정리하면, 나이지리아 연방법원이 야당 후보 아티쿠 아부바카르의 자격을 박탈했고, 그의 정당은 이 판결에 이의를 제기할 계획입니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

5.headline: Nigerian court strikes down Atiku's candidacy weeks before the vote
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.

Nigeria's already fraught road to its next presidential election took a dramatic turn on Thursday, when a federal judge in Abuja ruled that the leadership of the opposition African Democratic Congress had been illegally constituted. The decision, according to news reports, effectively strips former Vice President Atiku Abubakar of the party's presidential nomination.

The judgment went considerably further than a single candidacy. Nigerian outlets report that it nullified the emergence of the party's national officers and invalidated the nominations of every candidate the party had fielded for the 2027 elections, on the grounds that they flowed from an unlawful leadership.

The suit was brought from within the party's own ranks. One of its deputy national chairmen contended that, under the party's constitution, he ought to have assumed the leadership after the previous chairman stepped down, and the court granted the reliefs he sought. The party has vowed to appeal, and its officials, along with a chorus of critics, maintain that the case was engineered by the ruling party to hobble the opposition.
Litigation is nothing new for the coalition. Earlier this year, a court ordered the party deregistered altogether, only for an appellate court to reverse that ruling.

Mr. Abubakar is hardly a newcomer to such battles. A perennial contender, he has sought the presidency several times, most recently in 2023, when Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress prevailed in a hotly contested election. His removal from the race, even temporarily, therefore reshapes the field in a way few anticipated.

What makes this episode so consequential is its timing. As the Associated Press points out, the ruling lands roughly two months before polling day, in a country grappling with a battered economy and spiralling insecurity. A protracted legal battle could leave voters in limbo over who will actually appear on the ballot, and it hands the appeal courts an outsized role in shaping the contest for Africa's most populous nation.
To sum up, a federal court has thrown out Atiku Abubakar's candidacy and the party's entire slate, setting the stage for a high-stakes appeal just weeks before Nigerians vote.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스에 오신 것을 환영합니다.
이미 순탄치 않던 나이지리아의 차기 대선 가도가 목요일 극적인 전환을 맞았습니다. 아부자의 한 연방 판사가 야당 아프리카민주회의의 지도부가 불법으로 구성되었다고 판결한 것입니다. 보도에 따르면 이 결정으로 아티쿠 아부바카르 전 부통령은 사실상 이 정당의 대선 후보 지명을 잃게 됩니다.
판결은 한 사람의 후보 자격을 훨씬 넘어섰습니다. 나이지리아 언론에 따르면 법원은 이 정당 전국 지도부의 선출을 무효화하고, 2027년 선거에 내세운 모든 후보의 지명도 불법 지도부에서 나왔다는 이유로 무효로 했습니다.
소송은 당 내부에서 제기됐습니다. 전국 부대표 중 한 명은 당헌에 따라 전임 대표가 물러난 뒤 자신이 지도부를 맡았어야 했다고 주장했고, 법원은 그가 요청한 구제 조치를 받아들였습니다. 정당은 항소하겠다고 다짐했고, 당 관계자들과 여러 비판자들은 집권당이 야당을 무력화하려고 이 소송을 꾸몄다고 주장합니다.
이 연합 정당에 소송은 새로운 일이 아닙니다. 올해 초 한 법원은 이 정당의 등록을 아예 취소하라고 명령했지만, 결국 항소법원이 그 판결을 뒤집었습니다.
아부바카르에게 이런 싸움은 낯설지 않습니다. 단골 대선 주자인 그는 여러 차례 대통령직에 도전했고, 가장 최근에는 2023년에 출마했는데, 당시 치열한 접전 끝에 전진보회의의 볼라 티누부가 승리했습니다. 따라서 그가 일시적으로라도 경선에서 빠지면 선거 구도는 예상치 못한 방식으로 바뀌게 됩니다.

이번 일이 이토록 큰 파장을 낳는 이유는 시점입니다. AP 통신이 지적하듯 이번 판결은 투표일을 약 두 달 앞두고 나왔습니다. 나이지리아는 망가진 경제와 걷잡을 수 없이 악화하는 치안 불안과 씨름하고 있습니다. 법정 공방이 길어지면 유권자들은 실제로 누가 투표용지에 오를지 모르는 불확실한 상태에 놓일 수 있고, 아프리카 최대 인구 대국의 선거 판도를 정하는 데 항소법원이 지나치게 큰 역할을 하게 됩니다.
정리하면, 연방법원이 아티쿠 아부바카르의 후보 자격과 이 정당의 후보 명단 전체를 무효로 했고, 나이지리아 국민이 투표하기 불과 몇 주 전 중대한 항소전이 펼쳐지게 되었습니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

items.ko: 나이지리아 법원, 야당 대선 후보 무효

1.headline: Hong Kong activist gets ten more years in prison
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
Today's news is from Hong Kong. Joshua Wong is a famous young activist. An activist works hard for a cause, like more freedom.
He is already in prison. He was going to leave prison early next year. But on Thursday, a judge gave him ten more years.
The judge said he worked with other countries against Hong Kong. This is a crime under a security law. China made this law in 2020.
Joshua Wong is 30 years old. He became famous at a young age. He led student protests in 2014.
Some groups say the punishment is too hard.
Again, Joshua Wong must stay in prison for ten more years.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스입니다.
오늘의 뉴스는 홍콩 소식입니다. 조슈아 웡은 유명한 젊은 활동가입니다. 활동가는 더 많은 자유 같은 대의를 위해 열심히 일하는 사람입니다.
그는 이미 감옥에 있습니다. 그는 내년 초에 감옥에서 나올 예정이었습니다. 하지만 목요일에 한 판사가 그에게 10년을 더 선고했습니다.
판사는 그가 다른 나라들과 손잡고 홍콩에 맞섰다고 말했습니다. 이것은 한 보안법에 따른 범죄입니다. 중국이 2020년에 이 법을 만들었습니다.
조슈아 웡은 30살입니다. 그는 어린 나이에 유명해졌습니다. 그는 2014년에 학생 시위를 이끌었습니다.

Joshua Wong is now 30. He was already in prison for another case. He was going to be free early next year. Now he must stay much longer. According to news reports, he pleaded guilty. That means he said he did the crime. So the judge made the sentence a little shorter.
Mr Wong became famous as a teenager. He led student protests in 2014. Many people in Hong Kong also protested in 2019.
Human rights groups and Taiwan criticized the sentence. Hong Kong police welcomed it.
To sum up, Joshua Wong will spend ten more years in prison under the national security law.

3.headline: Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong sentenced to ten more years
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.

Today's story is from Hong Kong. Joshua Wong, one of the city's best-known democracy activists, has been sentenced to ten more years in prison. According to news reports, a Hong Kong judge handed down the sentence on Thursday.

The court found that Mr Wong colluded with foreign forces to endanger the city's security. To collude means to secretly work together with someone, often to do something wrong. Reports say the case was about asking other countries to put sanctions on Hong Kong and China. Sanctions are penalties, like blocking trade or freezing money. The charge falls under a national security law that Beijing imposed on Hong Kong in 2020.

Mr Wong, who is now 30, pleaded guilty, which means he admitted the charge. According to Euronews, the judge started from thirteen years and cut it to ten because of the guilty plea. Mr Wong was already in prison for another national security case. He had been expected to walk free early next year. Now his time behind bars will be much longer.
Mr Wong first became famous as a teenager, when he helped lead student protests in 2014. Huge protests followed in 2019, and the security law came the next year.
Reactions were divided. Hong Kong police welcomed the sentence. Human Rights Watch, a rights group, called it cruel and unjust, and Taiwan also criticized it.
To sum up, Joshua Wong will spend ten more years in prison for colluding with foreign forces.
Thank you for listening.

4.headline: Joshua Wong handed ten more years for foreign collusion
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.

Our top story this morning comes from Hong Kong, where prominent pro-democracy activist Joshua Wong has been sentenced to an additional ten years in prison. A judge at the city's High Court handed down the sentence on Thursday after Mr Wong pleaded guilty to colluding with foreign forces to endanger national security.

The charge falls under the national security law that Beijing imposed on Hong Kong in 2020. According to news reports, prosecutors accused Mr Wong of lobbying foreign governments and organizations to impose sanctions on Hong Kong and mainland China. Euronews reports that the judge set a starting point of thirteen years and reduced it to ten in recognition of the guilty plea, while noting that the offence was serious enough to carry a possible life sentence. His co-defendant, fellow activist Nathan Law, lives in self-imposed exile and remains wanted by the authorities.

The ruling comes just months before Mr Wong, now 30, had been scheduled to walk free after serving a sentence in a separate national security case. Instead, he now faces roughly another decade behind bars. In a letter to the court, Mr Wong reportedly said he had hoped to leave prison in 2027.

Mr Wong first rose to prominence as a teenage student leader during the 2014 Umbrella Movement, and he remained a visible figure through the mass protests of 2019. Hong Kong has since convicted scores of people under the security law, which critics say has been used to crush dissent.

Reaction to the sentence was sharply divided. A senior Hong Kong police official welcomed it, while Taiwan's mainland affairs authorities condemned what they called political persecution. Human Rights Watch described the sentence as cruel and unjust.
To sum up, Joshua Wong has received a further ten-year prison term for foreign collusion, extending his time in custody well into the next decade.
Thank you for listening.

5.headline: Joshua Wong jailed for another decade as Hong Kong crackdown grinds on
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.

Hong Kong's most recognisable young dissident will not be walking out of prison any time soon. On Thursday, a High Court judge sentenced Joshua Wong, the pro-democracy activist who first burst onto the scene as a schoolboy, to a further ten years behind bars for colluding with foreign forces to endanger national security.

Mr Wong had pleaded guilty to the charge, brought under the sweeping national security law that Beijing imposed on the city in 2020. According to news reports, the case centred on his efforts to lobby overseas governments and bodies to slap sanctions on Hong Kong and mainland China. Euronews reports that the judge, while stressing that the offence was grave enough to warrant life imprisonment, took thirteen years as his starting point and trimmed it to ten in light of the guilty plea. His co-defendant, fellow activist Nathan Law, remains in self-imposed exile overseas and is still wanted by the authorities; the court characterised the pair as the ringleaders of the scheme.

The timing is a cruel twist for the 30-year-old, who had been due for release early next year after completing a term in an earlier national security case. Instead, he is now looking at the better part of another decade in custody.

His trajectory mirrors that of the city itself. Mr Wong became the teenage face of the 2014 Umbrella Movement and remained a fixture of the vast street protests of 2019, which Beijing answered with the security law. Since then, scores of activists, journalists and opposition politicians have been prosecuted, and media tycoon Jimmy Lai was handed twenty years earlier this year under the same legislation.

The sentence drew predictably polarised responses. A senior official in the police national security department hailed it, whereas Taiwan's top body handling China policy decried what it described as endless political persecution. Human Rights Watch branded the ruling cruel and unjust and urged foreign governments to consider targeted sanctions in return.
To sum up, Joshua Wong has been handed an extra decade in prison for foreign collusion, underscoring how firmly Hong Kong's security apparatus continues to bear down on dissent.
Thank you for listening.

2.headline: Two US service members accused of mailing fake cannabis to Korea
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
Today's story is about two American service members in Korea. Korean customs officers say the two men smuggled drugs into the country. To smuggle means to bring something in secretly and illegally.

According to the customs office in Pyeongtaek, the drug was liquid synthetic cannabis. Synthetic means it is made in a lab. The drug was sent in March through the American military mail system. It was hidden in small containers inside protein supplement tubs.

An X-ray check found something strange in the package. One service member came to the post office at Camp Humphreys to pick it up. Officers arrested him there. The other man was the person the package was for. He was caught later.
Both men deny the charges. But customs officers say they found evidence on their phones. The case has now gone to prosecutors.
Camp Humphreys is a very large American base in Pyeongtaek. Customs also shared information about another possible drug case at an American base.
To sum up, two American service members are accused of smuggling synthetic cannabis into Korea through military mail.

오늘의 소식은 한국에 있는 미군 두 명에 관한 것입니다. 한국 세관 당국은 두 남성이 마약을 국내로 밀반입했다고 말합니다. 밀반입이란 무언가를 몰래, 불법으로 들여오는 것을 뜻합니다.

엑스레이 검사에서 소포 안의 이상한 것이 발견됐습니다. 군인 한 명이 그것을 찾으러 캠프 험프리스의 우체국에 왔습니다. 당국은 그 자리에서 그를 체포했습니다. 다른 한 명은 소포를 받을 사람이었습니다. 그는 나중에 붙잡혔습니다.
두 사람은 혐의를 부인합니다. 하지만 세관 당국은 그들의 휴대전화에서 증거를 찾았다고 말합니다. 이 사건은 이제 검찰로 넘어갔습니다.
캠프 험프리스는 평택에 있는 매우 큰 미군 기지입니다. 세관은 미군 기지에서 일어났을 수 있는 또 다른 마약 사건에 관한 정보도 넘겼습니다.
정리하면, 미군 두 명이 군사 우편을 통해 합성 대마를 한국에 밀반입한 혐의를 받고 있습니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

3.headline: Two US service members accused of smuggling synthetic cannabis by military mail
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.

Today's story is about drugs, the mail, and the American military in Korea. Korean customs officials say two American service members smuggled drugs into the country. To smuggle means to bring something across a border secretly and illegally.

According to news reports, the Pyeongtaek Customs Office announced the case on Wednesday. Officials say the drug was liquid synthetic cannabinoids. These are chemicals made in a lab that act like marijuana, and they are illegal in Korea. The drugs were sent in March through the American military postal system. They were hidden in small containers inside protein supplement tubs.

An X-ray scan showed something unusual in the parcel. Korean customs worked with American Army investigators on the case. One service member was caught when he came to collect the parcel at the military post office at Camp Humphreys. The second man, who was supposed to receive the package, was caught later.

Both men have been referred to prosecutors. Referred means the case is handed over so prosecutors can decide whether to charge them. One of them is being held in custody. The men deny the accusations. However, customs officials say they found supporting evidence on the men's smartphones.

Why does this matter? Camp Humphreys is the largest American military base overseas. The case shows that military mail can be used for smuggling. Customs also passed on information about another suspected case at an American base.
To sum up, two American service members are accused of mailing synthetic cannabinoids into Korea, and the case is now with prosecutors.
Thank you for listening.

4.headline: Customs refers two US service members to prosecutors over cannabinoid smuggling
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.

Two American service members stationed in South Korea have been referred to prosecutors on suspicion of smuggling synthetic cannabinoids into the country through the US military's own postal system. The Pyeongtaek Customs Office announced the case on Wednesday.

According to customs officials, the liquid drugs were shipped in March, concealed in small containers tucked inside tubs of protein supplements. The parcel was addressed to Camp Humphreys in Pyeongtaek. An X-ray screening flagged an irregular shape inside the package, prompting a joint investigation with US Army criminal investigators.

Officials say the first suspect was apprehended when he arrived to pick up the parcel at the base's military post office. The second suspect, identified as the package's intended recipient, was taken into custody later. One of the two has been referred to prosecutors under detention, while the other was referred without being detained.

Both men reportedly deny the allegations and have declined to cooperate with questioning. However, customs officials say a forensic analysis of their smartphones turned up evidence backing the charges. Synthetic cannabinoids are lab-made substances that mimic the effects of marijuana and are banned under South Korea's narcotics laws.

The case is drawing attention because it highlights how military mail can be exploited to move illegal goods. Customs officials say they have also passed information on a separate suspected synthetic cannabinoid case at a US base to Army investigators, suggesting the problem may not be isolated. Roughly 28,500 American troops are stationed in South Korea, and Camp Humphreys, home to the headquarters of US Forces Korea, is the largest American military base overseas.
To sum up, two US service members face possible charges for allegedly mailing synthetic cannabinoids into South Korea, and investigators are looking into at least one more suspected case.
Thank you for listening.

5.headline: Military mail exposed as smuggling route as two US troops face cannabinoid charges
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.

South Korean customs authorities say they have uncovered an attempt to use the US military's own postal network as a conduit for illegal drugs. Two American service members stationed in the country have been referred to prosecutors on suspicion of smuggling liquid synthetic cannabinoids, the Pyeongtaek Customs Office said on Wednesday.

According to officials, the shipment arrived in March, with small vials of the drug secreted inside tubs of protein supplements, a disguise apparently intended to slip past routine checks. It did not. An X-ray screening picked up an anomalous shadow in the parcel, which was bound for Camp Humphreys, the sprawling garrison in Pyeongtaek that is the largest American military installation overseas.

Rather than intercepting the package outright, Korean customs officers teamed up with US Army criminal investigators and, by local accounts, ran a controlled delivery. The first suspect was nabbed at the base post office as he came to collect the parcel; the second, its intended recipient, was tracked down subsequently. One has been referred to prosecutors in custody, the other without detention. Reports have not named the suspects, and no quantities or street values were disclosed.

Both men have reportedly denied wrongdoing and stayed silent under questioning, but officials maintain that a forensic examination of their smartphones yielded corroborating evidence. Synthetic cannabinoids, lab-made compounds engineered to mimic the effects of marijuana, are strictly prohibited under South Korea's narcotics legislation.

Beyond the individual case, the episode raises uncomfortable questions about oversight of military mail, which typically moves through channels separate from civilian post. Customs officials say they have already handed Army investigators information on another suspected synthetic cannabinoid case at a US base, hinting that this may be more than a one-off. Some 28,500 American troops are based in South Korea under the two countries' longstanding alliance, and incidents involving service members tend to attract intense public scrutiny here.

To sum up, two US service members are facing potential prosecution for allegedly mailing synthetic cannabinoids into South Korea, and the case has put the security of military postal channels under the spotlight.
Thank you for listening.
